brand.title: ESourceAIG (Production)
brand.subtitle: Knowledge Check — Getting Started with ESource Bookkeeping Tool

questions.question: What three things make this bookkeeping tool different from others?
choices: It carries your brand, your data stays with you, and everything is encrypted to your firm
It is free, it works offline, and it includes tax preparation
It connects to all banks automatically, it never needs backups, and it prepares tax returns
It requires no internet, it stores data in the cloud, and it shares data with accountants
questions.feedback_correct: Exactly right—your firm's brand appears on reports, bank data never leaves your computers, and encryption locks everything to your firm only.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The tool does require internet connection at least weekly to check in, does not prepare taxes, and keeps data on your firm's computers rather than in the cloud. Review Slide 2 to see the three key differences.

questions.question: How long does a 6-digit sign-in code remain valid after you receive it by email?
choices: Twenty minutes
Ten minutes
Five minutes
One hour
questions.feedback_correct: That's correct—the code works for ten minutes, so sign in promptly when you receive it.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The code expires after ten minutes, not five, twenty, or sixty. This timing protects your security by limiting the window someone could use an intercepted code.

questions.question: What should an owner do on the day a staff member leaves the firm?
choices: Ask the staff member to delete the tool from their computer
Remove them from the License tab so their computer locks at the next check-in
Wait until the end of the month to clean up their access
Change all the passwords on the client files
questions.feedback_correct: Correct—removing them the same day ensures their computer locks at the next check-in, protecting your client list.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Waiting until month-end leaves a security gap, and asking them to delete the tool trusts them to do so. The system automatically locks their access when you remove them from the License tab, even on a personal laptop.

questions.question: What five reports must you export from QuickBooks Online before switching a client to this tool?
choices: Chart of accounts, trial balance, open invoices, unpaid bills, and last year's ledger
Chart of accounts, bank reconciliation, customer list, vendor list, and journal entries
Trial balance, invoices, bills, tax summary, and profit and loss
Chart of accounts, cash flow, balance sheet, income statement, and tax returns
questions.feedback_correct: Perfect—those five reports give the tool everything it needs to set up the client's accounts and starting balances correctly.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The tool specifically needs the trial balance as of the day before the switch to establish opening balances, plus the chart of accounts, open invoices, unpaid bills, and last year's ledger. A switching guide shows exactly where to find each one in your old software.

questions.question: For banks other than Wells Fargo, which file formats work best for bank statements and why?
choices: CSV files are always best because they are smallest
Quicken or QuickBooks files work best because they include account number and balance
PDF files work best because they match Wells Fargo's format
OFX files work best because they encrypt the data
questions.feedback_correct: Right—Quicken and QuickBooks files include the account number and balance, which lets the tool verify the math automatically.
questions.feedback_incorrect: While CSV, OFX, and PDF are all acceptable formats, Quicken and QuickBooks files are preferred because they contain more complete information. If you upload a file without a balance, the tool will ask you for the ending balance.

questions.question: What does the AI do when you click "Suggest categories" on the Ask Client tab?
choices: It automatically categorizes all unsorted lines and updates your books
It groups similar unsorted lines and suggests a category with a reason for each group
It sends a message to your client asking them to categorize the transactions
It deletes all uncategorized transactions from the books
questions.feedback_correct: Exactly—the AI suggests a category and reason for each group, fills in the category menu, and nothing changes in your books until you accept.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The AI only suggests categories; it does not make changes automatically, send messages to clients, or delete transactions. You always review and accept before anything changes in your books.

questions.question: How should you set up a client's phone calendar reminder, and how often do you need to do it?
choices: Email the client a list of statements each month; repeat monthly
Text the client on the reminder day; repeat monthly
Download the calendar file and send it to the client once; their phone reminds them every month automatically
Call the client on the reminder day; repeat weekly
questions.feedback_correct: Perfect—you do this once per client, and then their own phone automatically reminds them every month.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The calendar reminder is set up just once. After the client taps the file and chooses Add, their phone takes over and reminds them every month in your firm's name without any action from you.

questions.question: What information is safe to share with the Need Help assistant, and what must you never share?
choices: You can share everything because the assistant is part of your firm's secure system
You can share client names and balances but not account numbers
You can ask how-to questions, but never share client names, account numbers, or balances because the assistant cannot see your books
You can only share information if you first get permission from your firm's owner
questions.feedback_correct: That's right—the assistant helps with how-to questions but has no access to your books, so client details must stay private.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The assistant cannot see your books or your screen, so sharing client names, account numbers, or balances would expose confidential information unnecessarily. Keep your questions focused on how-to steps and let the assistant guide you to the right tabs and buttons.

questions.question: According to the 3-2-1 backup rule, how should you store your backups and where should one copy be located?
choices: Keep one copy on your computer, one at your office on external storage, and one in the cloud
Keep three copies on two kinds of storage, with one copy kept away from the office
Keep backups only in the cloud and never on local computers
Keep backups on your computer and email one copy to your firm's owner monthly
questions.feedback_correct: Correct—three copies on two different types of storage, with one stored off-site, protects you against fire, theft, and computer failure.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The 3-2-1 rule is a professional backup standard: three copies, two different storage types (like computer and external drive), and one copy in a different location (like home if the office floods). This protects your client data comprehensively.

questions.question: When bringing in statements from PayPal or Stripe, why is uploading the activity CSV better than using a simple bank deposit record?
choices: The CSV file is smaller and uploads faster
The CSV captures full sales, fees, and refunds and prevents the tool from counting bank deposits twice
The CSV allows the tool to automatically categorize all transactions without your review
The CSV is required by law for payment processors
questions.feedback_correct: Exactly—the activity CSV shows the full detail (sales, fees, refunds) and the tool is smart enough not to double-count the deposit, giving you accurate books.
questions.feedback_incorrect: While the CSV file is useful, the real reason to use it is that it captures the complete transaction detail and prevents double-counting. Simply uploading a deposit record misses the fees and refunds, leaving your books incomplete.
